external_inputs: [6] Bansal-Sinha, Theorem 1.3 and Corollary 1.4 (checked against arXiv:2008.07003): randomized decision trees of error 1/3 for (2^{-5k},k)-Forrelation need Omega(k^{-29}(N/log(kN))^{1-1/k}) queries

lean.note: Statement.lean BansalSinhaLower unfolds to ∀ k≥2, ∃ t₀, ∀ t≥t₀, Lvalue k t < R(P k t). The theorem proves this proposition without a BansalSinhaLower hypothesis; its proof is the local alternative lower-bound route rather than the preprint’s citation.

adjudication_findings.claim: A main theorem proved under a BansalSinha hypothesis is conditional, not an unconditional verification.
adjudication_findings.reason: The ledger's alphaTot_eq_four takes hBS as a hypothesis. Its evidence class must say conditional on the published Forrelation bound.

adjudication_findings.claim: The imported Forrelation bound matches the gadget: normalisation, block length, delta, one-sided 1-case, absolute 0-case, error 1/3.
adjudication_findings.reason: Read directly. (1/N) z1^T(H Z2 ... H) zk equals u^T Dz1 H ... Dzk u. N=2^n covers m=4^t. Their tree measure is depth, the error is on each valid input (Section 5.4 p.38), matching def-R. Statement match only: see R1-AF-06a.

adjudication_findings.claim: The Bansal-Sinha lower-bound proof itself holds.
adjudication_findings.reason: No return re-proved it and neither did this adjudication. It is the single external mathematical input.

adjudication_findings.claim: eq-5 and eq-17 combine definitions with theorem conclusions.
adjudication_findings.paper_locus: Eq. 5, p.4 line 155; Eq. 17, p.12 line 597
adjudication_findings.reason: Both displays do define and assert. prop-4.2 depending on eq-17 and lem-2.1.i depending on eq-5 is circular at row level though not in the paper. Split; adjudicates against r3's alternative, see R3-DEP-04.

adjudication_findings.claim: BS numbering and promise; mu comes from minimax because p0,p1 have off-promise mass; pin v3.
adjudication_findings.reason: Read directly. Whether earlier versions were weaker was not checked; held copy is v3.

adjudication_findings.claim: Section 7: exact integer P; circuit size separate; persistent hypothesis L<R(P).
adjudication_findings.reason: Integer tests rederived. M-3 adds a constraint on the literal Corollary 1.4 form.

adjudication_findings.claim: The literal Bansal-Sinha statement holds only for large N depending on k.
adjudication_findings.reason: The ledger's BansalSinhaCor14 has the right order (absolute c, then k, then large n). A form with one threshold for all k is stronger than the proof gives. Also the printed term in their display reads delta^2/(4N) where their Theorem 3.1 gives 4/(delta^2 N); harmless for fixed k, no reliance on it here.

presentation.body: For each fixed $k\ge2$ and all sufficiently large powers of four $m$, $R(P_{k,m})>L$, where $L$ is defined in equation (5).
presentation.body_plain: For each fixed k ≥ 2 and all sufficiently large powers of four m, R(Pₖ,ₘ) > L, where L is defined in equation (5).
presentation.title: The randomized lower bound for Forrelation

statement: For fixed k>=2 and all sufficiently large powers of four m, R(P_{k,m})>L with L as in eq-5.
